correction.issued: the same session, on reading the two descriptors
correction.so_kernel_74_is: a granularity artifact, not a value divergence
correction.what_is_true: the eight is a PER-TOKEN LOOP, not a split reduction.  ROM's in0 is [6, 160] -- six contributions for ONE token -- dispatched once per token, and HBM's is [6, 128, 160], all 128 token rows batched into one dispatch.  Both reduce the same leading axis of six contributions, so each token receives the same pairwise tree.  The digests differ because they are digests of a [160] buffer against a [128, 160] one
correction.what_was_claimed: that kernel 74's disagreement was a reduction-association violation, because the graph declares pairwise_tree and the ROM lane spends eight operators on it against the HBM lane's one
correction.why_i_repeated_it: this is the FOURTH time this instrument has reported a lowering difference as a value one, and the tool's own docstring already warns about exactly this -- per-launch digests cannot compare lanes that dispatch differently.  I wrote that warning and then did not apply it

method: every engine dispatch's output views are digested against the descriptor's source_kernel_id -- the graph kernel both lanes were lowered from -- and the two traces are compared per kernel and then grouped by layer.  Digests only, because the lanes legitimately spend different NUMBERS of operators on one kernel and comparing (family, sub, digest) reports that as a value difference
not_a_claim: that the expert reduction is the ONLY divergence -- it is the first, and 1,087 of 1,317 shared kernels differ downstream of it
that fixing it makes either token match the oracle
question: the ROM wafer emits 2750 and the HBM single chip 459 from ONE graph over ONE set of weights.  Where do they stop agreeing?

result.reading: the prologue agrees completely.  Beyond it, this instrument cannot tell a granularity difference from a value one -- see the correction field

what_survives.not_sound: any claim about WHERE the values first diverge.  A disagreement between per-launch digests is ambiguous between granularity and value, and every disagreement this trace reports is at a kernel where the lanes dispatch differently
what_survives.sound: the PROLOGUE AGREEMENT.  Identical digests imply identical bytes and identical shapes, so the prologue's kernels genuinely produce the same results in both stores: token ids, embedding, compressed-id map and hyper-connection expansion

what_would_settle_it: digest each kernel's whole declared OUTPUT TENSOR after its last launch retires, not each launch's own view.  That is shape-independent by construction and is the instrument this question needs; it is named in the tool's docstring and still not built
why_this_is_not_the_engram_gate: the gate was the other candidate and is now excluded: both stores run the same engine, and executing the release's own gate instead of the frozen v1 contract left both tokens unchanged (2750, 459)
